newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish shares track overseas down, thin, eye Fed.
newsitem.headline: Finnish shares track overseas down, thin, eye Fed.

text.p: Shares ended cautious trade broadly lower on Monday, tracking overseas markets which held their breath ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee Meeting due on Tuesday, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 0.55 percent to 2,127.21 with volume a light 250 million markka, one-third of it in Nokia which fell 0.80 markka to 194.00, matching early dealings on Wall Street.
"No one wants to do anything until the outcome of the Fed meeting is known," one broker said.
Forestries also slid in line with the overall market, except UPM-Kymmene, which closed 0.30 markka up at 98.00, helped by brisk overseas demand, brokers said.

But UPM's engineering subsidiary Rauma lost 1.00 markka at 94.50 in fair trade. Rauma said earlier it had sold its U.S. pipeline inspection company Vetco, but the deal would not have a noteable effect on Rauma's 1996 results.
Food, animal feeds and chemicals group Raisio closed active trade 4.00 markka up at 275.00 on bargain-hunting after a slump on Friday.
The company denied a report in Friday's New York Times that new products from Campbell's Soup of the U.S. may rival its low-cholesterol Benecol margarine. Raisio said the products would not compete.
